title: Do Most New Businesses Really Fail in a Few Years?
question: Do most new businesses really fail within a few years?
alternates: How Long Does the Average New Business Actually Last?
The Survival Curve Behind 'Most Businesses Fail'
premise: The BLS survival table says 79.6% of establishments opened in 2015 survived one year, 61.4% three, 50.2% five and 34.7% ten, so about half close within five years and two-thirds within ten. 'Most fail within a few years' overstates it; exits include sales and relocations, not only failures; and there is no breakdown for online stores. Taylor's second-hand SBA and NFIB figures agree on the shape.
whyWatch: The failure statistic is quoted both to discourage and to sell; the official survival table says something more precise.
tension: 'Most fail within a few years' against a curve where half are still open after five.

arc.hook: Nine in ten businesses fail: where does that number come from?
arc.evidence: The BLS cohort survival curve, what an 'exit' includes, and the absence of online-store data.
arc.resolution: About half within five years, two-thirds within ten; 'most within a few years' is wrong, 'most eventually' is right.
arc.takeaway: Quote the curve, not the slogan.

evidence.note: BLS defines an establishment as a single economic unit such as a store or factory, typically at one physical location, in contrast to a firm or company, which may consist of one or more establishments; establishment survival counts places of business, not businesses.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.note: BLS age and survival data are measured at the establishment level, not the firm level: a chain store's new branch is a new opening for the establishment tables though only an expansion for the firm, so the survival tables are not a business failure rate.
evidence.why: the verdict note limits its own scope ("though")

evidence.note: A BLS closing is an establishment that had positive employment and then reports none (or zero) in the current quarter; the definition records that payroll employment stopped at that unit, not why, so an exit is not necessarily a failure.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded
